idiom_name: hand-written association-table mapper (statements in an RAII transaction scope)
implementation_notes: C++ ships no standard persistence layer, so the link table is declared and written by hand: a table with the two foreign keys and a composite primary key, and mapper functions that add or remove a link inside an RAII transaction guard so a failure rolls the whole association update back. The composite key replaces what an ORM would generate; std::vector or std::unordered_set on each side is just the in-memory collection the mapper has to reconcile with the table. Code-generating ORMs such as ODB exist for C++ but are not the default in most code bases, and a hand-written mapper stays preferable where the build should not gain a code generator.
pitfalls: A mapper that writes the link table without a transaction can leave half the association applied when a statement fails mid-way.
The in-memory collection must be the owner of the truth for the diff; sharing one vector between two actors and mutating it from both sides writes the same link twice or loses one.
Raw pointers to the associated objects make lifetime the caller's problem: store ids or owning handles on the association side, or the mapper writes links for objects that are already gone.
Exceptions must not escape a destructor doing rollback; keep the guard noexcept and report the original error.
